subject: How to get results for data of interest only when fitting detection function with additional data

messages.author: 3ccd0ce7a0e754ad
messages.subject: How to get results for data of interest only when fitting detection function with additional data
parts:
Hello,

I want to run an analysis based on only 37 detections. Because of the recommended 80 minimum detections, I have added additional detections from another geographic area (but same methods and habitat type) to estimate the detection function. I have treated these detections as a separate stratum and also have several strata within the data set of interest. 

The "summary" function provides a population estimate, SE, and CV for the total and for each individual stratum. The problem is that I need a total population estimate/SE/CV for my area of interest only (not including the additional data I used to help with the detection function . I realize that I can calculate the total population estimate by summing the estimates of each stratum, but how to I get the SE and CV?

I hope this was clear and thanks for any advice anybody is able to provide.

Laurel

messages.author: 54c94f7c2bf78491
messages.subject: Re: How to get results for data of interest only when fitting detection function with additional data
parts:
Hi Laurel, 

You can produce the total for selected strata only by setting the Area of the other strata to 0. This will then include those strata in fitting the detection function, but not in the estimates of density and abundance.


In the attached image, the detection function would be based on all 6 strata, whilst the abundance estimate would be for the sum of strata 3 and 4 only.

Olly

messages.subject: Re: How to get results for data of interest only when fitting detection function with additional data
parts:
Thanks to Eric for pointing out you are probably using the R package.

In this case, the process depends on if you are using the flatfile format (all data in a single table) or if you have a seperate table for each level of data (i.e. a region.table, a sample.table, a obs.table, and a dataframe with your observations).

For the latter, you can use something like this:

subset.region.table <- region.table # make a copy of your region table
subset.region.table $Area[subset.region.table $Region.Label != "MyStratum1" | subset.region.table $Region.Label != "MyStratum2"] <- 0 # Set the value of Area to 0 for all strata except your strata of interest, using an "or" operator to retain the area in more than one stratum. In this case, your abundance estimate will be the sum of MyStratum1 and MyStratum2.

If you are using a flatfile format, the idea would be the same, with slightly difference implementation. I don't have a code example, but it'll be very similar - find all instances of strata you want to use in the DF but not in the estimate, and set their Area values to 0. 

Your output will look something like this:

## Abundance:
##     Label  Estimate       se        cv       lcl       ucl       df
## 1    2010   0.00000   0.0000 0.0000000  0.000000   0.00000  0.00000
## 2  2011_H   0.00000   0.0000 0.0000000  0.000000   0.00000  0.00000
## 3  2011_L   0.00000   0.0000 0.0000000  0.000000   0.00000  0.00000
## 4    2013   0.00000   0.0000 0.0000000  0.000000   0.00000  0.00000
## 5  2014_H   0.00000   0.0000 0.0000000  0.000000   0.00000  0.00000
## 6  2014_L   0.00000   0.0000 0.0000000  0.000000   0.00000  0.00000
## 7  2016_H  20.73131  15.1065 0.7286803  5.360042  80.18359 22.21659
## 8  2016_L 108.49847 111.4174 1.0269027 18.691301 629.80736 22.24405
## 9    2018   0.00000   0.0000 0.0000000  0.000000   0.00000  0.00000
## 10  Total 129.22979 113.5590 0.8787368 27.114194 615.92604 23.91076

In this case, line #10 is an abundance estimate summed from strata 7 and 8, but using all strata for the detection function. (Note, this is horrible data with huge CVs! Just an example of summing strata...)

For density, the Total line will be the mean density, rather than summed.

I am posting this here instead of making a new thread because I have a very similar issue as Laurel did but in opposite form. I have estimated the detection function from pooled duplicate data that occurred during combined double platform effort from dedicated and transit transect legs and now would like to apply it to only my dedicated transect leg data which includes the majority of my detections which occurred on solo primary platform effort. I have 34 total detections on dedicated legs - 10 of which are duplicates that were used to fit the detection function and 24 are from solo primary platform effort. 

This is a line transect ship survey for a dolphin species with attractive responsive movement to the boat. My tracker platform was a visual observer team and my primary platform is a towed hydrophone array. I will be applying the mean group size from visual detections to estimate abundance. My current issue is that I cannot find a way to subset either the obs.table or region.table in a way that allows me to apply the detection function from my duplicate data to all of my detections on dedicated legs. I have spent multiple days trying to find a way around this - the best I can do thus far is get dht to create a table with perfect values for area, covered region, effort, and k. For 'n' it only provides the values and cv's of the object ID numbers that were 9 of the 10 duplicates as these were the ones that occurred on dedicated legs. (The 10th was a tracker only sighting and I am not sure if I can include this in my abundance estimate.) 

I have 3 survey strata: Region 1 = 8 clusters, Region 2 = 18 clusters, Region 3 = 8 clusters  that were detected on dedicated legs. 
This is the closest I have been able to get to the correct output:

Hi All,

Just want to give an update that my problem has been solved by a friendly distance user! If anyone else runs into this issue please feel free to email me. The issue was resolved through a couple steps in reformatting the csv file: 1) duplicate data used to estimate the detection function contained detections from both dedicated and transit legs. The transit duplicate detections need to be labeled as their own region 'X' and set the area of this region to zero. 2) the single platform primary detections on dedicated legs that were collected when only the primary platform effort was working need to be arranged just like the duplicate data with 2 rows per detection. Here, observer 2 (tracker) will always equal zero and observer 1 will always equal 1. The detected column needs to match this. 3) Lastly, an extra column named whatever you want needs to be added and all rows of duplicate data need to be populated with a 1 and all rows of single platform detections (2 rows per detection) need to be populated with zeros. Treat this column as a factor variable. 

Since all of my detections that occurred on dedicated legs when only one effort platform was working happened to occur on the primary platform, the detection function ignored these in the estimate because they were never seen by the tracker. I compared my DF model results using my prior data set up to this one and they are identical. :)  Further, abundance is not estimated for the duplicate detections that occurred on transit legs (Region 'X') and these appear in the final table output as zeros and are not incorporated into the estimates. 

My one question that remains regards how to appropriately incorporate the cv of my mean group size value into the cv for D and N. My group size column is only populated with the mean arithmetic group size for all detections (calculated from visual sightings on effort within my truncation distance which are not size biased by distance) thus, my variance is showing up as zero for group size and is not incorporated into my variance estimate. I have selected to estimate the empirical variance for density using Innes et al. 2002 based on an R2 estimator because I am applying the same detection function and group size value to all 3 of my strata. If it is ok to estimate variance based on the delta method for these data please let me know. I am finding the equations to estimate variance for clusters in Marques and Buckland, 2004 quite difficult to follow. 

My mean group size = 3.52, se= 0.81, cv = 0.23 

This is my current output for D and N in DISTANCE:

Any advice will be much appreciated, I am very happy to be at this stage of the analysis! So close! 
Best,
Morgan
